name: Planetary System Navigation & Exploration Foundation
particleExperimentIntegrator: bounded semi-implicit Euler with mode-specific substeps
cosmicPhenomena: white-dwarf and brown-dwarf physical lab presets
compactObjectSafety: propulsion-safe stand-off + adaptive strong-gravity steps + black-hole/neutron-star model guards + 10% c speed guard
cosmicObservation: massless frame/orbit views + physical bounded-thrust rendezvous to anchored phenomena
flightComputer: propulsion-safe target-relative approach with braking-safe velocity envelope + persistent station-keeping hold + STOP RELATIVE + TURN & BURN + physical inertial brake + prograde/retrograde attitude aids
fragmentPolicy: max 2 primary resolved fragments, 16 total resolved impact fragments, family cascade suppression
navigationNumerics: adaptive strong-gravity physics substeps + 10% c Newtonian validity guard
observationCamera: massless experiment/cosmic frame-track-orbit views with ship-state isolation
experimentNavigation: selected experiment fields + physical bounded-thrust rendezvous
spaceWeather: directional kinematic CME cones with explicit speed, arrival geometry, automatic seeded events, no MHD/radiation damage model, and save/load timeline continuity
scientificOverlays: target-centric approximate L1-L5 + Hill sphere + Roche limit + instantaneous orbital plane + live Newtonian gravity-vector samples
transitDrive: explicitly fictional spacecraft-only FRAME translation with swept massive-body clearance; ordinary celestial integration remains authoritative; manual exit matches target inertial velocity and supported normal body arrivals use an exit-only circular-orbit insertion calculation
boostDrive: explicitly speculative bounded 5,000 m/s² local propulsion mode; manual BOOST selection drops time warp to 1×
experimentLifecycle: active/complete lifecycle + retained final observation bounds + deterministic replay + active-particle-only 60× warp cap with safe restore
velocityVector: ship-view inertial velocity-direction HUD marker, separate from nose/reticle attitude
stellarRendering: layered seeded photosphere/granulation + additive corona + filament prominences + active regions + rare visual flare proxies
stellarPerceptualLod: preserve macro stellar phenomena at distance; reduce only sub-pixel/noisy micro detail and shift emphasis into scale-appropriate halo/prominence cues
stellarExposure: gentle apparent-angular-size exposure adaptation with close-star background suppression; HUD remains unaffected
transitArrivalVisual: short exponential release of fictional FRAME FOV/streak cues after disengage/arrival; physical Newtonian position and velocity are unchanged
systemMap: mobile-first live star → planet → moon navigation catalog with LOG SURVEY non-linear discovery view, TRUE SYSTEM linear inertial X/Z view, and TRUE LOCAL linear selected-planet/moon-family view; all modes read authoritative N-body positions and never create a second orbit model
discovery: persistent 0-3 layered scan depth per cosmic source; classification, signal/stability detail and final scientific/fictional status unlock progressively
anomalyLayer: 9-15 deterministic seeded free-space anomaly signals per system spanning speculative, anomalous and intentionally impossible/fictional reality classes; visuals never secretly become gravity sources
surfaceFoundation: three seeded landing regions on the first landable home planet, with deterministic terrain/environment identities, local first-person exploration, persistent scans, explicit descent/landed/ascent/orbit lifecycle and guarded boarding-based takeoff
surfacePhysicsBoundary: while landed, authoritative major-body N-body gravity continues at a forced 1× through the existing velocity-Verlet path while ShipDynamics/navigation are surface-constrained and not integrated; surface anomalies still do not create hidden gravity, teleportation or time effects; atmospheric entry/aerodynamics, fluid weather, rigid-body surface physics and ecosystems remain future layers
surfacePersistence: optional schema-1 surfaceSession payload preserves body/region identity, local x/z/yaw/pitch, scanned/selected POIs, local weather timeline, and a backward-compatible body-fixed landing anchor with capture time/model version; selected landing region, cockpit preference, pre-surface simulation running state and orbital time scale remain optional backward-compatible fields
cockpitView: default-on low-obstruction camera-attached Three.js cockpit with four translucent smoked-glass CanvasTexture MFDs (NAV/FLIGHT/SCIENCE/SYSTEM DIAGNOSTICS), a right-side ship-mounted diagnostics pane with a slimmed physical bezel/projector rail, compact lower-right thrust/reverse/brake overlay clear of the diagnostics panel on iPhone landscape, functional physical keys, touch ray-picking, subtle emissive cockpit/status lighting, observation/surface auto-hide, optional user toggle, and schema-1 cockpitEnabled preference persistence
surfaceWeather: persistent deterministic local surface-weather clock remains separate from SimulationClock; ordinary and impossible presentation events affect visibility/readouts only, not aerodynamic force or damage; weather can continue locally even when celestial astronomy is paused
landedShip: upgraded lightweight spacecraft exterior with smoother hull, canopy, swept wings, twin engines, VTOL thrusters, landing gear, nav/strobe/landing lights, landing beacon and distance/boarding readout; visual surface representation remains separate from authoritative orbital ship physics while landed
surfaceHud: compact-by-default mobile exploration HUD with persistent expanded/collapsed state, always-available scan/sprint controls, details-only save/takeoff controls, and landed-only SKY PAUSE/RESUME plus body-fixed lat/lon, rotation phase, primary-star altitude/azimuth and geometric local solar-time diagnostics
landingLifecycle: explicit ORBIT -> DESCENDING -> LANDED -> ASCENDING -> ORBIT state machine with transition locking, near-ship boarding requirement, scripted VTOL descent/ascent visuals, cleanup-before-ORBIT commit, forced live-flight restoration, prograde return attitude, held-input reset, multi-frame orbital render verification and recovery fallback instead of half-transitioned states
landingRecovery: surface entry/ascent failures clean up renderer/UI/session state and fall back to a valid orbital state; successful takeoff force-restores running 1x ship flight, neutral input state and prograde attitude, then requires multiple verified orbital render frames before success
ascentHandoff: surface renderer ownership detaches before disposal; ASCENDING cleanup commits ORBIT only after local state is gone; held pointer controls are force-released; the ship returns in body-relative prograde attitude; three orbital frames render at zero simulation dt before ASCENT COMPLETE is announced; invariant misses recover without tripping the animation-loop fault latch
takeoffPhysicalDiagnostics: temporary compact ascent/orbit telemetry retained for iPhone Safari/WebKit release testing; renderer/backend and runtime performance/debug telemetry remain visible in ship view through the integrated SYSTEM DIAGNOSTICS cockpit MFD and remain available in the ordinary top HUD when the cockpit is hidden
rendererBackendPolicy: WebGPURenderer remains the renderer family; iPhone/iPad-class WebKit forces its WebGL2 backend at boot for physical presentation-handoff isolation, while other platforms keep automatic WebGPU/WebGL2 selection; no live backend hot-swap
astronomicalObserver: one read-only canonical observer derives inertial position, look/local horizon bases, parent/anchor/altitude, simulation time and live major-body directions for ship, descent and surface modes; landed local-up/east/north now derive from a rotating body-fixed landing anchor when rotation metadata is available
skyContinuity: one deterministic inertial star catalog is reused in space and on surfaces; landed horizon projection is dynamically reprojected against the rotating body-fixed observer without reseeding or deleting catalog entries; atmospheric/daylight/weather visibility remains presentation-only
celestialApparentSize: physical range and apparent angular radius remain separate from bounded rendering proxy size
surfaceSkyTime: landed major-body celestial time advances at forced 1× when running and can now be explicitly paused/resumed from the surface DETAILS HUD; local exploration/weather remain separate and responsive while paused
magnetarPlacement: repeated LAB magnetars use deterministic golden-angle collision-safe offsets; gravity remains Newtonian and magnetic/MHD forces remain unmodeled
cockpitInteraction: every visible cockpit screen and physical key is functional; NAV opens the System Map, FLIGHT opens the existing Flight/System controls, SCIENCE opens Science, and SYSTEM DIAGNOSTICS now opens a dedicated read-only Engineering/Diagnostics drawer instead of duplicating Flight/System; cockpit inputs dispatch existing app actions without duplicating simulation authority
cockpitAssetStrategy: procedural modular shell carried forward from v0.1.4.6.1.2; the diagnostics MFD is procedural CanvasTexture/geometry with no external cockpit asset, and presentation/control interfaces remain isolated so a later optimized GLB cockpit can replace the shell without rewriting flight/science systems
cockpitLighting: mobile-safe emissive-only panel accents plus live POWER/TARGET/NAV/PROPULSION/CAUTION indicators; no additional dynamic cockpit lights or physics state
cockpitDiagnostics: live renderer, FPS, physics/render time, ship speed, simulation time, seed, major/test counts, draw calls, prediction time and experiment telemetry are mirrored into the right-side translucent ship-mounted MFD and a dedicated read-only Engineering/Diagnostics drawer; the values remain sourced from existing app/renderer state and own no simulation authority
frameDrive: tap-toggle speculative spacecraft-only translation toward a locked body/COSMOS target; real-time frame-rate tiers step down near arrival; world N-body/particle simulation authority is untouched; local ship acceleration is suspended while active; manual disengage matches the target inertial velocity, while normal planet/moon/rogue-planet completion may hand off into a calculated circular osculating orbit before ordinary ShipDynamics/gravity resume
assetCachePolicy: HTML shell version-tags styles.css and src/main.js with build tag 148; main/app/renderer/system-map module hops are also version-tagged so Safari/GitHub Pages do not mix the v0.1.4.8 shell with stale cockpit/navigation JavaScript.
planetaryRotation: deterministic body-fixed rigid rotation foundation for generated planets/moons using independent per-body RNG streams, inertial spin axes, periods, phases/epochs and body-fixed landing anchors; rotation metadata does not consume or perturb the legacy orbital-system RNG sequence
surfaceAstronomyDiagnostics: read-only surface DETAILS diagnostics derive from the same canonical astronomical observer and rotation model used by rendering: procedural body-fixed latitude/longitude, rotation phase, primary-star altitude/azimuth, and geometric local solar time from primary-star hour angle; no independent sky model or physics authority
planetaryNavigation: generated stars, planets and moons are first-class selectable NAV targets from the authoritative body registry with live range, parent, radius, mass, gravity, Kepler-period, eccentricity, rotation, Hill-radius, surface-capability and atmosphere-model diagnostics
frameOrbitArrival: normally completed FRAME travel to planets, moons and rogue planets hands back to Newtonian flight in a calculated instantaneous circular osculating orbit when a resolved window exists inside 47% of a conservative Hill-radius screening estimate based on the smaller of live separation and orbital pericenter; this is not a long-term N-body stability guarantee
landabilityFoundation: NAV classifies current detailed surface capability separately from physical body type: rocky/moon bodies may remain solid but orbital-only, gas giants report no solid surface, and atmosphere physics is explicitly unmodeled rather than inferred from artwork
frameSafetyRouting: deterministic live-body-anchored FRAME detours are used only when a direct swept segment would intersect another massive-body clearance guard; candidate bypass legs are checked against every massive-body guard, guard radii are never reduced, and celestial states are never moved by the route planner
